title: DDRoute: a Novel Depth-Driven Approach to the Qubit Routing Problem
problem: Qubit routing compilation in NISQ devices inserts SWAP operations to satisfy topological constraints, but current heuristics produce circuits with incompatible depth overhead for hardware limits.
motivation: Current quantum device depth limits prevent execution of deeply compiled circuits; reducing routing-induced depth is critical for near-term quantum computing.
method: Qubit routing places quantum bits (qubits) on a quantum computer's physical layout to satisfy interaction constraints, typically by inserting SWAP operations that move qubits to compatible positions. DDRoute solves this routing problem using a depth-driven heuristic: when choosing where to place each SWAP, it selects the position that reduces circuit depth—the total number of sequential operations—the most. This contrasts with existing methods that try to balance multiple competing objectives like minimizing SWAPs while also reducing depth.
key_novelty: The core idea is optimizing qubit routing by prioritizing circuit depth—the number of sequential operations—over other objectives, achieving up to 70% depth reduction compared to existing methods.
contributions: Achieves up to 70% circuit depth reduction vs state-of-the-art routing
Depth-driven optimization improves compatibility with NISQ device constraints
More efficient qubit mapping for near-term quantum processors
Enables execution of deeper quantum circuits within hardware depth limits
limitations: Not discussed; limited to NISQ-era devices.
primary_theme: Depth-optimized qubit routing for NISQ circuits
